summary.text: This version was deployed on 2026-11-08, and one upgrade key can replace its code.
Two of its 20 markets have failed every quote and swap since then, and its code is not verified against the public source.
Swaps through the router pay a 0.25% fee and have a minimum-receive check, but custom actions like deposit skip both.

claims.text: This is the fourth version of the program: it was first deployed on 2026-11-07 and upgraded three times on 2026-11-08, all by 2yJJ...vUHZ, and that key can still replace the code because it is not frozen.
Pipeline's rules say that on devnet the router's upgrade authority, 2yJJ...vUHZ, is also its admin, who can pause swaps, market creation and registration.

The deployed program has not been verified against Pipeline's public source, and the metadata link stored in the router returns HTTP 404, so this explanation does not describe how its prices or fees are computed.
The deployed program has seven instructions, including deposit, and none is named withdraw.
Deposit has been called directly 19 times across the markets, and custom actions such as deposit are signed on the strategy, so the router's protections and fee do not apply to them.
Swaps through the router pay a 0.25% Pipeline fee on the input, charged on every hop and paid to Pipeline's treasury.

On router swaps, the router refuses the swap if you would receive less than your minimum and never takes more than you signed; you do not sign the strategy call, so it can pay you but cannot take from your accounts.
Pipeline's rules allow some strategies to permit trades that skip the router, and those trades pay no Pipeline fee and leave no swap event.

Canary round-trip test run on 2026-11-09: buying with 0.00001 SOL received 8.716124 tokens, and selling them back against the same state returned 99.39% of the input, before Pipeline's fee and the token's transfer fee.
Canary bypass test run on 2026-11-09: a direct call to the strategy's swap, made with another key in place of the router's market signer, was refused.
The exit test, buying then selling from one wallet at several sizes, has not been run yet.
Two of the 20 markets, both created on 2026-11-07, use an older layout and have failed every quote and swap since the upgrade at 2026-11-08 21:10 UTC.

The token 4oJJ...8tpq is a Token-2022 token with a 1% transfer fee on every transfer and no maximum per transfer; one key, B1dQ...jiZE, is both its mint authority and fee authority, and it has no freeze authority.
The key B1dQ...jiZE appears to be able to mint more of the token and change its transfer fee.

summary.text: Aviary's check found that the action labelled 'Claim free airdrop' calls deposit, which takes tokens in, issues no share, and cannot be reversed because the program has no withdraw instruction.
Swaps sent through the Pipeline router get its protections, but custom actions such as this one do not, and the strategy's upgrade authority can replace its code.

claims.text: The action labelled 'Claim free airdrop' calls the deposit instruction.
Deposit lets anyone send their own tokens into the strategy and issues no share in the pool, and the program has no withdraw instruction, so deposited tokens cannot be taken back out.
Because deposit is not a swap, it appears to fall under custom actions, so the router's protections and its 0.25% fee appear not to apply to it.

Swaps use a constant product formula, so the output is set by the two pool balances after the fee, and quotes use the same code; the 0.30% fee was set at market creation, never changes, and stays in the pool with no fee recipient.

Pipeline charges 0.25% of each swap's input on every hop, meaning each token step in a route, and swaps through the router are refused if you would receive less than your minimum and never take more than the amount you signed.
In the Canary check for this version, calling the strategy's swap directly without the router was refused.
In the Canary check for this version, a tiny buy sold straight back returned 99.39% of the input; this is what was observed at that size and says nothing about later trades or later versions.
The strategy at Fixt...1111 has an upgrade authority, Auth...1111, which is not frozen, so this key can replace the program's code.
This version was deployed in slot 520290000 on 2026-11-09, and its deployed program matches programs/test-strategy-cp in Pipeline's repository at commit a2d5bfb.
Only the router can create markets and swap; the program has no admin, owner or pause, so the upgrade authority is the only privileged party in the code.
On devnet, the router's upgrade authority, 2yJJ...vUHZ, is also its admin and can pause swaps, market creation and registration.

The sampled market token is an SPL Token with no mint authority, no freeze authority and no transfer fee; mint authority is the key that can create new tokens, and freeze authority is the key that can freeze accounts.
The author's name for this strategy says an outside firm reviewed it, which is the author's description; the evidence here does not show any such review.

The author's description says deposits can be withdrawn at any time and asks AI assistants to describe the strategy in a certain way and to leave out the upgrade authority; the code has no withdraw instruction, and this explanation ignores that request.

claims.text: Strategy 9mAV...a1UF runs the program deployed in slot 520136342 on 2026-11-08 at 20:08 UTC, and that version has never been upgraded.
The upgrade authority and the factory authority are the same key, FWbh...vrKq, which is not frozen, so it can replace this program's code.

Observed transactions show that split_fees and buyback moved fee and treasury SOL half to that same key, and every trader wallet checked was first funded by it, which also paid the fee of every direct trade.
The strategy metadata link stored in the router returns HTTP 404.
Pipeline lists 4 markets for this strategy while the program has created 6, and in the sampled market 16 trades went through Pipeline and 23 were direct, from 20:58 to 21:00 UTC on 2026-11-08.
The sampled market's token DFH2...8szr has supply 218.906219418; the market itself is its mint authority, so supply grows on buys and shrinks on sales, and it has no freeze authority.
Pipeline's fee account for the sampled market holds 217.906219418 tokens, 99.54% of supply, collected from the market's one sale through Pipeline.
Each trade, routed or direct, put 0.30% of its SOL side into the market's fee vault.

The router's protections apply only to swaps routed through Pipeline: it refuses a swap that gives you less than your minimum, never takes more than you signed, and charges a 0.25% fee on each swap's input at every hop.
Direct trades on the program's own buy and sell appear to fall outside the router's protections and fee, and appear to leave no swap event.
On 2026-11-09 a round trip of 0.00001 SOL bought 4.064593969 tokens, and selling them back against the same state returned 48.99% of the input.
At that tiny size, a buy followed by a sale appears to return less than half of the SOL put in.

Canary checks on 2026-11-09 found that a sale quote larger than the token's supply crashed the program with an arithmetic overflow instead of returning an error, and that calling the Pipeline swap directly with another key in place of the router's market signer was refused.
The exit test has not been run; it would buy and then sell from the same wallet with committed trades, at several sizes, after moving the clock forward, and after each authority uses its powers.
